condition_name: Productive Cough & Common Cold (Kaphaja Kasa & Pratishyaya)
remedy_name: Tulsi-Adrak-Madhu Swarasa (Holy Basil, Ginger & Honey Juice)
remedy_text: Take 5-10 ml fresh juice of Tulsi (Ocimum sanctum) leaves mixed with 2-5 ml fresh Adrak (ginger) juice and 1 teaspoon (5 ml) of unheated Madhu (honey) twice or thrice daily after meals. For children (ages 5-12), use half the adult dose.
ayurvedic_note: Tulsi and Ardraka possess Katu-Tikta Rasa and Ushna Virya, which liquefy tenacious Kapha in the Pranavaha Srotas (respiratory tract), pacify Vata, and relieve bronchial spasm. Madhu acts as a Yogavahi (bio-enhancer) and Kaphahara vehicle. Never boil or heat honey.
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Lukewarm water (Ushnodaka), light Yusha (moong soup). Apathya: Cold water, curd (Dadhi), fried/heavy foods, daytime sleep (Divaswapna).
source: Ayurvedic Home Remedies (CCRAS, Govt. of India), p. 1 (Adrak) & p. 25 (Tulsi); Ashtanga Sangraha Chikitsasthana Ch. 4
safety_check: Contraindicated in Infants under 1 year (Honey) and Severe Hyperacidity/Peptic Ulcer (Ginger)

condition_name: Dry Irritative Cough & Throat Tickle (Vataja Kasa)
remedy_name: Dalchini-Elaichi-Kalimirach Churna with Ghee & Honey
remedy_text: Option A: Chew a small piece of Dalchini (Cinnamomum zeylanicum) bark or 1-2 Elaichi (Elettaria cardamomum) pods slowly to soothe throat irritation. Option B: Mix 1 gm Kalimirach (Black pepper) powder or 500 mg Elaichi powder with 1/2 tsp Ghee (clarified butter) and 1 tsp Madhu (honey); lick slowly twice daily.
ayurvedic_note: In Vataja Kasa, dryness (Rukshata) in the throat causes paroxysmal dry coughing. Ghee lubricates the mucosal lining (Snehana), while Maricha, Tvak, and Ela clear subtle Srotorodha and calm Udana Vata.
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Warm milk with a pinch of turmeric and ghee, warm soups. Apathya: Dry, cold, astringent snacks, cold air exposure.
source: Ayurvedic Home Remedies (CCRAS), p. 5 (Dalchini), p. 7 (Elaichi), p. 13 (Kalimirach); Chakradatta Kasachikitsa
safety_check: Avoid Black Pepper in active Peptic Ulcer; avoid Honey in Infants under 1 year

condition_name: Recurrent Cold, Allergic Rhinitis & Sinus Congestion (Peenasa / Pratishyaya)
remedy_name: Dhania-Jeera-Haldi-Methi Herbal Decoction (Kwatha)
remedy_text: Boil 5 gm crushed Dhania (coriander seeds), 2 gm Jeera (cumin), 1 gm Haldi (turmeric) powder, 1 gm Methi (fenugreek) seeds, and a pinch of black pepper in 160 ml water until reduced to 40 ml (one-fourth). Filter and drink warm twice daily. Alternatively, take 2 gm Haldi powder in warm milk twice daily to prevent allergic attacks.
ayurvedic_note: Haridra is a premier anti-allergic (Kaphavatahara and Vishaghna) herb in Madanapala Nighantu, while Dhanyaka and Jiraka kindle digestive Agni (Deepana-Pachana) to stop the formation of Ama that fuels recurrent rhinitis.
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Warm water, steam inhalation, light warm meals. Apathya: Cold drinks, ice cream, banana, curd at night, dust/cold wind exposure.
source: Ayurvedic Home Remedies (CCRAS), p. 6 (Dhania), p. 9 (Haldi), p. 12 (Jeera); Madanapala Nighantu Abhayadi Varga
safety_check: Safe across all adult groups including Hypertension and Gastritis (omit pepper if ulcer is active)

condition_name: Nasal Blockage & Frontal Sinus Headache (Nasaavarodha & Kaphaja Shiroroga)
remedy_name: Ajvain Steam Inhalation (Bashpa Sweda) & Warm Forehead Lepa
remedy_text: 1) Nasal Blockage: Add 1-2 gm crushed Ajvain (Trachyspermum ammi) seeds to steaming hot water and inhale the medicinal vapours 2-3 times a day. 2) Sinusitis Headache: Prepare a warm paste of Ajvain powder (or Sonth powder) with a little water and apply externally over the forehead and slightly below the eyes (avoiding direct eye contact) in the morning.
ayurvedic_note: Yavani (Ajvain) contains thymol-rich volatile oils with Tikshna, Ushna, and Kapha-Vatahara properties (Madanapala Nighantu). Steam inhalation (Bashpa Sweda) liquefies impacted Kapha in the paranasal sinuses (Shringataka Marma).
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Warm water, covering head and ears in hill winds. Apathya: Cold water head bath, daytime sleeping.
source: Ayurvedic Home Remedies (CCRAS), p. 1 (Adrak) & p. 2 (Ajvain); Ashtanga Sangraha Uttarasthana Ch. 24
safety_check: External & steam application — safe for all comorbidities; keep paste away from eyes

condition_name: Hoarseness of Voice, Sore Throat & Laryngitis (Swarabheda & Kanthashobha)
remedy_name: Sonth-Kalimirach Ghee-Honey Linctus & Laung Chew
remedy_text: Option A: Mix 1-2 gm powder of Kalimirach (Black pepper) fried in Ghee, or 1-3 gm dry Sonth (ginger) powder with honey; keep in the mouth and swallow slowly 2-3 times daily. Option B: Chew 1 Laung (clove) or take 20 ml warm decoction prepared from 1 gm clove 3-4 times daily.
ayurvedic_note: Swarabheda occurs when Vata and Kapha obstruct the Swarvaha Srotas (vocal cords). Fried Maricha with Ghee and Lavanga clear Kapha coating while Ghee pacifies local Vata.
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Voice rest, warm saline or turmeric water gargles (Kavala). Apathya: Loud speaking, cold water, sour pickles, curd.
source: Ayurvedic Home Remedies (CCRAS), p. 1 (Sonth), p. 13 (Kalimirach), p. 16 (Laung); Chakradatta Swarabheda Chikitsa
safety_check: Avoid Sonth/Kalimirach in severe Peptic Ulcer; use Elaichi/Dalchini instead

condition_name: Chronic Cough, Bronchitis & Cold with Fever (Kasa, Shwasa & Jwara)
remedy_name: Pippali-Sunthi-Maricha (Trikatu) Decoction & Honey Linctus
remedy_text: 1) Cold with Fever / Cough: Take 2 gm Pippali (Piper longum) powder with 1 tsp honey twice or thrice daily in divided doses. 2) Bronchial Cough: Prepare 10-20 ml decoction from 2-3 gm coarse powder of Pippali, dry ginger (Sunthi), and black pepper (Maricha); take warm with honey or sugar 2-3 times a day.
ayurvedic_note: Pippali is a premier Rasayana for the Pranavaha Srotas (lungs) with Madhura Vipaka and Anushna-Sheeta / Ushna potency (Madanapala Nighantu, Ashtanga Sangraha). Trikatu digests Ama and clears Kapha-Vata obstruction in the bronchi.
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Old rice (Purana Shali), Kulattha (horse gram) soup, warm water. Apathya: Cold drinks, heavy dairy, fish, refrigerated food.
source: Ayurvedic Home Remedies (CCRAS), p. 23 (Pippali); Bhaishajya Ratnavali Jwaradhikara v. 108 (Pippali Kwath)
safety_check: Contraindicated in active Peptic Ulcer, Pregnancy (high dose Pippali), and Infants under 1 year (Honey)

condition_name: Subacute Cough, Allergic Bronchitis & Chest Congestion (Kasa & Shwasa)
remedy_name: Sitopaladi Churna (Classical 5-Ingredient Respiratory Powder)
remedy_text: Combine Sitopala (rock candy/misri - 16 parts), Vamshalochana (bamboo manna - 8 parts), Pippali (long pepper - 4 parts), Ela (cardamom - 2 parts), and Tvak (cinnamon - 1 part) into a fine powder. Take 1-3 gm mixed with 1 tsp honey and 1/2 tsp Ghee twice or thrice daily after meals.
ayurvedic_note: Classical formulation from Chakradatta and Bhaishajya Ratnavali. Unlike purely pungent formulations, Sitopaladi Churna balances Vata, Pitta, and Kapha simultaneously—relieving both dry/burning cough (Pittaja/Vataja) and productive cough without aggravating gastric acidity.
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Warm milk, pomegranate, light digestible diet. Apathya: Cold beverages, sour/fermented foods.
source: Chakradatta Rajayakshma Chikitsa (p. 86); Bhaishajya Ratnavali Kasarogadhikara
safety_check: Avoid in uncontrolled Diabetes (contains Sitopala/Misri) and Infants under 1 year (Honey)

condition_name: Productive Cough, Asthma, Sinusitis & Anorexia (Kaphavata Kasa, Shwasa & Aruchi)
remedy_name: Talisadi Churna / Modaka (Classical Respiratory & Digestive Formula)
remedy_text: Prepared from Talisa patra (Abies webbiana - 1 part), Maricha (2 parts), Sunthi (3 parts), Pippali (4 parts), Vamshalochana (5 parts), Ela (1/2 part), Tvak (1/2 part), and Sharkara (sugar - 32 parts). Take 2-3 gm with honey twice daily after food.
ayurvedic_note: Extolled in Ashtanga Sangraha (Chikitsasthana Ch. 7, p. 363) and Chakradatta (p. 86) for Kasa (cough), Shwasa (dyspnea/asthma), Aruchi (loss of appetite), Chhardi (vomiting), and Grahani.
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Lukewarm water, light warm meals. Apathya: Heavy, oily, cold foods.
source: Ashtanga Sangraha Chikitsasthana Ch. 7 (p. 363); Chakradatta (p. 86)
safety_check: Contraindicated in uncontrolled Diabetes (contains Sharkara) and severe Peptic Ulcer

condition_name: Bronchial Asthma, Wheezing & Productive Cough (Shwasa & Kaphaja Kasa)
remedy_name: Vasa Swarasa / Vasavaleha (Malabar Nut Leaf Juice / Linctus)
remedy_text: Take 10 ml fresh expressed juice (Swarasa) or 20 ml decoction of Vasa (Adhatoda vasica / Adusa) leaves mixed with 1 tsp honey and a pinch of Pippali powder twice daily. Or take 5 gm classical Vasavaleha twice daily with warm water or milk.
ayurvedic_note: Vasa (Atarusha) is declared in Ashtanga Sangraha (Sutrasthana Ch. 13 Agryasangraha, p. 97) and Chakradatta (p. 86) as supreme among Kapha-Pitta shamaka and bronchodilator herbs. It dilates airways and expels thick sputum.
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Warm water, light diet. Apathya: Smoke, dust, cold air, curd.
source: Ashtanga Sangraha Chikitsasthana Ch. 3-4 (p. 339-345); Chakradatta (p. 86); Madanapala Nighantu Abhayadi Varga
safety_check: STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATED IN PREGNANCY (Vasa has uterotonic/oxytocic activity)

condition_name: Pediatric Cold & Cough (Bala Kasa & Pratishyaya)
remedy_name: Safed Pyaj (White Onion) Decoction with Jaggery
remedy_text: For children above 1 year with cold and cough: Prepare a mild decoction from a small piece of white onion (Allium cepa / Palandu) in water, mix with a small amount of Jaggery (Guda), and give 5-10 ml thrice daily.
ayurvedic_note: Palandu (white onion) is Madhura-Katu, Snigdha, and Kapha-Vatahara without aggravating Pitta excessively (Ashtanga Sangraha Sutrasthana Ch. 7, p. 55). Gentle expectorant for children.
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Warm clothing, lukewarm water. Apathya: Cold milk, banana, curd.
source: Ayurvedic Home Remedies (CCRAS), p. 22 (Pyaj)
safety_check: Avoid jaggery in diabetic patients; safe for children >1 year

condition_name: Hiccoughs & Spasmodic Diaphragm Irritation (Hikka)
remedy_name: Elaichi Chew & Kalimirach-Misri / Laung-Madhu Yoga
remedy_text: Option A: Chew 1-2 fruits of Elaichi (Green Cardamom) frequently (up to 4 per day). Option B: Take 1-2 gm Kalimirach (black pepper) powder with sugar/misri twice daily, or 1-2 gm Laung (clove) powder with honey in three divided doses.
ayurvedic_note: Hikka arises from upward-moving (Pratiloma) Prana and Udana Vata mixed with Kapha. Elaichi and Lavanga pacify Vata spasm in the diaphragm and stomach cardia (Anulomana).
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Sips of lukewarm water, calm breathing. Apathya: Hurried eating, dry/chilly foods, carbonated drinks.
source: Ayurvedic Home Remedies (CCRAS), p. 7 (Elaichi), p. 13 (Kalimirach), p. 16 (Laung); Ashtanga Sangraha Chikitsasthana Ch. 6
safety_check: Elaichi option is safe for all including Pregnancy and Gastritis; avoid Kalimirach in Ulcer

condition_name: Acute Sore Throat, Tonsillitis & Pharyngitis (Kanthashobha / Tundikeri)
remedy_name: Warm Haldi-Sendha Namak & Anar Rind Decoction Gargle (Kavala)
remedy_text: Option A: Boil 1/2 tsp Haldi (turmeric) powder and 1/2 tsp Sendha Namak (rock salt) in 200 ml water; gargle warm 3-4 times daily. Option B: Boil 10 gm dried Anar (Punica granatum) fruit rind in 200 ml water until reduced to 50 ml; gargle warm 3-4 times a day.
ayurvedic_note: Kashaya-Tikta gargles (Kavala/Gandoosha) reduce mucosal edema (Shotha), clear Kapha-Rakta congestion in the pharynx, and exert local antimicrobial action without systemic blood-pressure elevation (safe in Hypertension where Mulethi is avoided).
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Warm liquid diet, voice rest. Apathya: Cold water, sour curds, fried snacks.
source: Ayurvedic Home Remedies (CCRAS), p. 3 (Anar) & p. 9 (Haldi); Ashtanga Sangraha Uttarasthana Ch. 26 (Mukharoga Pratishedha)
safety_check: Safe across all comorbidities including Hypertension, Pregnancy, and Diabetes

condition_name: Acute Viral Fever & Coryza (Nava Jwara / Vata-Kapha Jwara)
remedy_name: Tulsi-Dhania Kwath (Holy Basil & Coriander Fever Decoction)
remedy_text: Boil a handful (10-15) fresh Tulsi leaves and 5 gm crushed Dhania (coriander seeds) in 120 ml water until reduced to 30 ml. Filter and drink warm thrice a day. Alternatively, prepare 20 ml decoction from 5 gm Dhania powder with a little sugar 3-4 times a day.
ayurvedic_note: In Nava Jwara (acute fever), Swedana (diaphoresis) and Ama-Pachana (digesting toxins) are primary. Tulsi induces gentle sweating to break Vata-Kapha fever, while Dhanyaka relieves internal burning (Antardaha) and thirst (Trishna) without aggravating Pitta.
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Langhana (light fasting or thin rice gruel/Manda/Peya), boiled warm water. Apathya: Heavy meals, milk/ghee in acute Ama stage, daytime sleep, cold bath.
source: Ayurvedic Home Remedies (CCRAS), p. 6 (Dhania) & p. 25 (Tulsi); Bhaishajya Ratnavali Jwaradhikara v. 15
safety_check: Safe for all patients; omit sugar if diabetic

condition_name: Fever with Thirst, Burning Sensation & Dehydration (Pittaja Jwara & Trishna)
remedy_name: Shadanga Paniya (Classical Six-Herb Medicated Fever Water)
remedy_text: Take equal parts of Musta (Cyperus rotundus), Parpataka (Fumaria indica), Ushira (Vetiveria zizanioides / Khus), Chandana (Santalum album), Udichya/Sugandhabala (Pavonia odorata), and Nagara/Sunthi (dry ginger). Boil 10 gm (1 Karsha) coarse powder in 640 ml water until reduced to 320 ml (half). Cool and give in small sips throughout the day whenever thirsty.
ayurvedic_note: The gold-standard classical fever hydration formula from Bhaishajya Ratnavali (Jwaradhikara v. 34-36, p. 24-25), Chakradatta, and Ashtanga Sangraha (Chikitsasthana Ch. 1, p. 325). It digests Ama (Amapachana), quenches morbid thirst (Trishna), and clears Pitta fever.
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Laja Peya (parched rice gruel), Moong Yusha. Apathya: Spicy, sour, fried foods, exertion in sun.
source: Bhaishajya Ratnavali Jwaradhikara v. 34-36 (p. 24-25); Ashtanga Sangraha Chikitsasthana Ch. 1 (p. 325); Chakradatta Jwarachikitsa
safety_check: Universally safe across all ages and comorbidities

condition_name: Prolonged, Intermittent or Recurrent Fever (Vishama Jwara & Jirna Jwara)
ayurvedic_disease_name: Vishama Jwara / Jirna Jwara / Sannipata Jwara
remedy_name: Guduchyadi Kwath & Sudarshana Churna
remedy_text: 1) Guduchyadi Kwath: Prepare 20-30 ml decoction from equal parts of Guduchi (Giloy - Tinospora cordifolia), Nimba bark (Neem), Dhanyaka (Coriander), Padmaka, and Raktachन्दन; take twice daily. 2) Sudarshana Churna (Kiratatikta-predominant 54-herb powder): Take 2-3 gm with warm water twice daily after meals for recurrent or chronic fevers.
ayurvedic_note: Described in Bhaishajya Ratnavali (Jwaradhikara v. 87-90 & v. 293-303, p. 37-38 & 89-90) and Ashtanga Sangraha. Guduchi and Kiratatikta are Tikta Rasa, Agnideepana, and Jwaraghna without causing constipation or dryness, clearing deep-seated Dhatugata Jwara and hepatosplenomegaly.
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Old rice, Moong dal soup, pomegranate, warm water. Apathya: Heavy grains, curd, daytime sleep.
source: Bhaishajya Ratnavali Jwaradhikara v. 87 (p. 37) & v. 293-303 (p. 89-90); Ashtanga Sangraha Chikitsasthana Ch. 1-2
safety_check: Safe in Hypertension, Diabetes, and Gastritis; use under medical supervision if fever >3 days

condition_name: Sunstroke, Heat Exhaustion & Dehydration (Anshughata & Trishna)
remedy_name: Nimbu Shikanji, Nariyal Pani & Dhania Hima
remedy_text: Option A: Squeeze 1 fresh Nimbu (lemon) into a glass (200 ml) of water with a pinch of rock salt and 1 tsp sugar; sip frequently. Option B: Drink tender coconut water (Nariyal pani) 2-3 times daily. Option C: Take 20 ml decoction/cold infusion of 5 gm coarse Dhania powder with sugar and a pinch of salt frequently. Include white onion (Pyaj) in meals to prevent sunstroke.
ayurvedic_note: Narikela Jala is Snigdha, Swadu, Hima (cooling), Laghu, and Pitta-Anila Hara (Ashtanga Sangraha Sutrasthana Ch. 6, p. 40). Nimbu with Lavana and Sharkara rapidly restores electrolytes and Prana.
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Cool shade, wet cloth sponging, coconut water, buttermilk. Apathya: Hot sun exposure, alcohol, tea/coffee, spicy fried food.
source: Ayurvedic Home Remedies (CCRAS), p. 6 (Dhania), p. 19 (Nariyal), p. 21 (Nimbu), p. 22 (Pyaj); Ashtanga Sangraha Sutrasthana Ch. 6 (p. 40)
safety_check: Omit added sugar in Diabetes; omit added salt in severe Hypertension

condition_name: Indigestion, Sluggish Digestion & Loss of Appetite (Agnimandya, Ajirna & Aruchi)
remedy_name: Adrak-Saindhava / Adrak-Guda Pre-Meal Appetizer
remedy_text: Take 5 gm fresh crushed Adrak (ginger rhizome) mixed with a pinch of Saindhava Lavana (rock salt) or Jaggery (Guda) twice daily 15-30 minutes before meals. Alternatively, take a pinch of Hing fried in ghee with a crushed piece of Adrak in a glass of buttermilk before food.
ayurvedic_note: Praised in Ashtanga Sangraha (Sutrasthana Ch. 7, p. 58) and Bhavaprakasha ('Bhojanagre sada pathyam lavanardrakabhakshanam'): Ginger and rock salt taken before meals clear tongue coating (Jihva Vishodhana), stimulate Pachaka Pitta and Samana Vata, and digest Ama.
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Eating only when hungry, warm freshly cooked food, buttermilk (Takra). Apathya: Overeating (Atimatrashana), eating before previous meal is digested (Adhyashana), cold water during meals.
source: Ayurvedic Home Remedies (CCRAS), p. 1 (Adrak) & p. 10 (Hing); Ashtanga Sangraha Sutrasthana Ch. 11
safety_check: Contraindicated in Hyperacidity, Gastritis, Peptic Ulcer, and Raktapitta (Bleeding disorders)

condition_name: Indigestion & Post-Meal Heaviness (Safe for Pitta / Mild Gastritis)
remedy_name: Jeera-Saunf-Saindhava Churna or Anar Swarasa
remedy_text: Option A: Take 3-5 gm powder of roasted Saunf (fennel) and fried Jeera (cumin) with a pinch of rock salt in warm water thrice daily after meals. Option B: Take 10 ml fresh Anar (pomegranate) juice with 1 gm black salt or fried Jeera powder and honey/sugar before food.
ayurvedic_note: Unlike pungent ginger or pepper, Shatapushpa (Saunf), Jiraka (Jeera), and Dadima (Anar) kindle Jatharagni (Deepana) while remaining gentle on Pitta (Anushna). Ideal for patients who have both indigestion and mild acidity.
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Light meals, buttermilk with roasted cumin. Apathya: Fried, stale, and fermented foods.
source: Ayurvedic Home Remedies (CCRAS), p. 3 (Anar), p. 12 (Jeera), p. 24 (Saunf)
safety_check: Safe in Hyperacidity and Pregnancy; omit rock salt if severe Hypertension

condition_name: Flatulence, Bloating, Gas & Colicky Abdominal Pain (Adhmana, Atopa & Vataja Shoola)
remedy_name: Ajvain-Saunf Churna & Hing-Takra / Nabhi Lepa
remedy_text: 1) Oral for Gas/Pain: Take 2 gm Ajvain powder mixed with 2 gm Saunf powder with warm water twice or thrice daily; OR take 1 gm Hing fried in ghee mixed in a glass of buttermilk twice daily; OR take 5 ml ginger juice in a glass of buttermilk with lemon and salt. 2) External for Infant/Child Colic & Distension: Dissolve a pinch of Hing in warm water and apply around the navel (umbilicus).
ayurvedic_note: Hingu is declared in Ashtanga Sangraha (Sutrasthana Ch. 13 Agryasangraha, p. 98: 'Hinguniryasah chedaniyadipaniyanulomikavatakaphaprashamananam') as the foremost herb for Vata-Anulomana (downward movement of trapped gas) and relieving colic (Shoolaghna).
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Warm water, Asafoetida-tempered moong dal, light meals. Apathya: Chickpeas (Chana), kidney beans (Rajma), potatoes, raw salads, cold drinks.
source: Ayurvedic Home Remedies (CCRAS), p. 1 (Adrak), p. 2 (Ajvain), p. 10 (Hing); Ashtanga Sangraha Sutrasthana Ch. 13 (p. 98)
safety_check: Avoid oral Hing in Pregnancy and severe Peptic Ulcer (external navel paste is safe for infants/children)

condition_name: Chronic Gas, Indigestion, Abdominal Colic & Sluggish Bowels (Vata-Gulma & Agnimandya)
remedy_name: Hingvashtaka Churna (Classical Eight-Ingredient Carminative Powder)
remedy_text: Composed of equal parts of Sunthi, Maricha, Pippali, Ajmoda (Apium graveolens), Saindhava Lavana (rock salt), Shweta Jeeraka (white cumin), Krishna Jeeraka (black cumin), and 1/8th part Ghee-fried Hingu. Take 1-2 gm mixed with the first morsel of warm rice and 1/2 tsp Ghee at the beginning of meals twice daily.
ayurvedic_note: Classical formulation from Bhaishajya Ratnavali (Agnimandyadi Rogadhikara) and Ashtanga Sangraha (Chikitsasthana Ch. 16 Gulma Chikitsa, p. 414). Taken with the first morsel of food and ghee, it kindles Jatharagni and prevents post-prandial bloating and colic.
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Warm freshly cooked meals with a little cow's ghee, buttermilk. Apathya: Heavy legumes, cold water, irregular meal times.
source: Ashtanga Sangraha Chikitsasthana Ch. 16 (p. 414); Bhaishajya Ratnavali Agnimandyadhikara
safety_check: Contraindicated in Pregnancy, Hyperacidity/Peptic Ulcer, and uncontrolled Hypertension (contains Saindhava)

condition_name: Hyperacidity, Heartburn, Acid Reflux & Peptic Ulcer (Amlapitta & Parinama Shoola)
remedy_name: Amla Churna with Milk, Nariyal Pani & Jeera-Ghee
remedy_text: 1) Amla Yoga: Take 3-5 gm Amla (Emblica officinalis) fruit rind powder or 10-20 ml fresh Amla juice twice daily with milk. 2) Nariyal & Anar: Drink tender coconut water (Nariyal pani) or 10 ml sweet Anar juice twice daily. 3) Jeera-Ghee: Boil 5-10 gm Ghee with 1-2 gm Jeera and take with warm rice during meals.
ayurvedic_note: Amalaki has Amla Rasa but Madhura Vipaka and Sheeta Virya (Ashtanga Sangraha Sutrasthana Ch. 18, p. 116: 'Prayo amlam pittalam anyatra dadimamalakat' — sour substances generally increase Pitta except Pomegranate and Amla!). It neutralizes Vidagdha Pitta and heals mucosal ulcers.
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Old rice, barley (Yava), bitter gourd (Patola), pomegranate, cold milk, ghee. Apathya: Chili, garlic, hing, sour curd, fermented foods, tea/coffee, fasting, anger/stress.
source: Ayurvedic Home Remedies (CCRAS), p. 3 (Anar), p. 4 (Amla), p. 12 (Jeera), p. 19 (Nariyal); Ashtanga Sangraha Sutrasthana Ch. 18 (p. 116)
safety_check: 100% Safe in Hyperacidity, Peptic Ulcer, Hypertension, and Pregnancy

condition_name: Severe Hyperacidity, Sour Belching & Biliousness with Constipation (Urdhwaga Amlapitta)
remedy_name: Avipattikara Churna (Classical Pitta-Pacifying Antacid & Mild Laxative)
remedy_text: Composed of Trikatu, Triphala, Musta, Vida Lavana, Vidanga, Ela, Patra (1 part each), Lavanga (11 parts), Trivrit (Operculina turpethum - 44 parts), and Sharkara (sugar - 66 parts). Take 3-5 gm with cool or lukewarm water twice daily before meals or at bedtime.
ayurvedic_note: Classical formulation from Bhaishajya Ratnavali (Amlapittadhikara). In Amlapitta, Virechana (downward elimination of excess Pitta via Trivrit) is the definitive treatment. Avipattikara neutralizes gastric acid and clears Pitta through gentle bowel movement.
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Cooling diet, coconut water, sweet fruits, milk. Apathya: Spicy, sour, fried foods, late-night meals.
source: Bhaishajya Ratnavali Amlapittadhikara; Ashtanga Sangraha Kalpasthana Ch. 2 (p. 465)
safety_check: Contraindicated in Pregnancy (contains Trivrit purgative), Diarrhea, and uncontrolled Diabetes (contains Sharkara)

condition_name: Nausea, Vomiting & Morning/Motion Sickness (Chhardi & Hrillasa)
remedy_name: Nimbu-Kalimirach Sip, Dalchini-Madhu & Elaichi-Ghee Yoga
remedy_text: Option A: Mix 5-10 ml fresh Nimbu (lemon) juice with water, a little sugar, and a pinch of rock salt; sip frequently in small quantities. Option B: Take 250-500 mg Elaichi seed powder fried in Ghee with honey thrice daily, OR 1-2 gm Dalchini powder with honey in divided doses.
ayurvedic_note: Nimbu and Elaichi calm rebellious Udana Vata and Kapha-Pitta in the Amashaya (stomach), restoring normal downward peristalsis (Anulomana) and stopping emesis (Chhardi-nigrahana).
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Laja Manda (parched paddy water), pomegranate juice, smelling lemon/cardamom. Apathya: Heavy, greasy, foul-smelling foods.
source: Ayurvedic Home Remedies (CCRAS), p. 5 (Dalchini), p. 7 (Elaichi), p. 21 (Nimbu); Ashtanga Sangraha Chikitsasthana Ch. 8 (p. 366)
safety_check: Safe in Pregnancy (morning sickness) and Gastritis; avoid honey in infants <1 year

condition_name: Acute Mild Diarrhoea & Loose Motions (Atisara)
remedy_name: Bhuna Jeera-Saunf Takra (Roasted Cumin & Fennel Buttermilk) & Anar Decoction
remedy_text: 1) Buttermilk Yoga: Mix 1-2 gm roasted Jeera (cumin) powder and 3-5 gm Saunf (fennel) powder in 250 ml fresh churned buttermilk (Takra); take 3-4 times daily. 2) Pippali-Takra: Mix 2-3 gm Pippali powder in 1 litre buttermilk, divide into 4 parts, and take 1 part every 6 hours. 3) Anar Rind: Take 10 ml decoction of Anar (pomegranate) fruit skin thrice daily.
ayurvedic_note: Takra (buttermilk) is Laghu, Kashaya-Amla, Deepana, and Grahi (absorbent/stool-binding) as taught in Ashtanga Sangraha (Sutrasthana Ch. 6, p. 41 & Chikitsasthana Ch. 11-12). Dadima rind is strongly Kashaya (astringent) and Stambhana, checking fluid loss while preserving Agni.
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Peya/Vilepi (rice gruel), buttermilk, pomegranate, boiled water. Apathya: Milk, heavy/oily foods, leafy greens (Shaka), wheat, sugary drinks.
source: Ayurvedic Home Remedies (CCRAS), p. 3 (Anar), p. 12 (Jeera), p. 23 (Pippali), p. 24 (Saunf); Bhaishajya Ratnavali Atisaradhikara
safety_check: Safe across all adult groups; ensure oral rehydration if stools are frequent

condition_name: Pediatric Diarrhoea & Colicky Loose Motions (Bala Atisara)
remedy_name: Jayphal (Nutmeg) Rubbed Paste & Elaichi Skin Ash
remedy_text: 1) For Children: Rub Jayphal (Myristica fragrans / Nutmeg) fruit on a clean stone with a little water or mother's milk/boiled milk (1 pinch, ~125-250 mg) and give 3-4 times a day. 2) For Abdominal Pain due to Diarrhoea in Adults: Take 1-2 gm Jayphal powder with warm water, or 2 gm ash of Elaichi skin with a little honey 4-5 times a day.
ayurvedic_note: Jatiphala is Grahi (absorbent), Deepana, and reduces intestinal hypermotility (Sangrahi) while calming Vata colic and irritability in children.
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Breast milk (for infants), rice water (Tandulodaka), pomegranate juice. Apathya: Heavy cow/buffalo milk, solid heavy foods.
source: Ayurvedic Home Remedies (CCRAS), p. 7 (Elaichi) & p. 11 (Jayphal); Ashtanga Sangraha Uttarasthana Ch. 2 (Balamaya Pratishedha)
safety_check: Do not exceed recommended pinch dose of Jayphal in children; avoid honey in infants <1 year

condition_name: Dysentery with Mucus/Blood, IBS & Malabsorption (Pravahika, Raktatisara & Grahani)
remedy_name: Kutajadi Kwath / Kutajavaleha & Bilvadi Churna
remedy_text: 1) Kutajadi Kwath: Prepare 20-30 ml decoction from Kutaja bark (Holarrhena antidysenterica), unripe Bilva fruit pulp (Aegle marmelos), Musta, Dhataki flowers, and Dadima rind; take twice daily with 1 tsp honey. 2) Home Dysentery Diet: Eat white onion (Pyaj) chopped and fried in Ghee with cooked white rice.
ayurvedic_note: In Ashtanga Sangraha (Sutrasthana Ch. 13, p. 98: 'Kutajatvak shleshmapittaraktasangrahaniyopashoshananam'), Kutaja and unripe Bilva are declared the supreme Sangrahika (anti-dysenteric and mucosal-healing) herbs for Pravahika, ulcerative colitis, and Grahani.
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Old red/white rice with buttermilk or ghee-fried white onion, Bilva sherbet. Apathya: Spicy, leafy, or fibrous raw foods, milk.
source: Bhaishajya Ratnavali Atisaradhikara v. 35-36 (p. 281) & Grahanyadhikara; Chakradatta Atisarachikitsa (p. 31-35); Ayurvedic Home Remedies (CCRAS), p. 22
safety_check: Do not use astringent Stambhana in the first 24 hours of acute infectious Ama diarrhea without Amapachana (use Dhanyapanchaka first)

condition_name: Constipation & Hard Stools (Vibandha & Koshtha-Baddhata)
remedy_name: Ghee-Warm Milk Bedtime Yoga (Snehana Anulomana) or Amla-Milk / Triphala Churna
remedy_text: Option A (Safe for All, including Pregnancy): Put 5 ml (1 tsp) cow's Ghee in a cup of warm milk with a little sugar/munakka and drink at bedtime; OR take 3-5 gm Amla powder with warm milk twice daily. Option B (Non-Pregnant Adults): Take 3-5 gm Triphala Churna (equal parts Haritaki, Vibhitaki, Amalaki) with lukewarm water at bedtime.
ayurvedic_note: Dryness (Rukshata) of Apana Vata in the Pakwashaya (colon) causes Vibandha. Warm milk with Ghee lubricates the colon (Mridu Коshtha Snehana), while Triphala provides gentle Anulomana and Rasayana action (Ashtanga Sangraha Sutrasthana Ch. 12, p. 94).
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Warm water throughout the day, fiber-rich vegetables, soaked raisins (Draksha), papaya. Apathya: Dry/roasted snacks, suppressing natural urges (Vega-dharana), late-night waking (Ratri-jagarana).
source: Ayurvedic Home Remedies (CCRAS), p. 4 (Amla) & p. 8 (Ghee); Ashtanga Sangraha Sutrasthana Ch. 12 (p. 94)
safety_check: Triphala/Haritaki is contraindicated in Pregnancy (use Ghee + Warm Milk or Amla instead)

condition_name: Hemorrhoids / Piles — Dry & Bleeding (Shushka & Raktaja Arsha)
remedy_name: Ajvain-Kala Namak Takra (for Dry Piles) & Anar Rind Yoga (for Bleeding Piles)
remedy_text: 1) Non-Bleeding / Dry Piles (Vata-Kapha Arsha): Take 1 gm Ajvain powder and 1 gm black salt (Kala Namak) in a glass of buttermilk (Takra) twice daily after meals. 2) Bleeding Piles (Raktarsha): Take 10 ml fresh Anar (pomegranate) juice with sugar twice a day, OR 10 gm dry Anar fruit rind powder with an equal quantity of sugar twice a day.
ayurvedic_note: In Ashtanga Sangraha (Chikitsasthana Ch. 10 Arsha Chikitsa, p. 382: 'Takram hi paramaushadham anilakaphotthitanam'), Takra (buttermilk) is revered as the supreme medicine for Vata-Kapha piles as it restores Agni and shrinks pile masses, while Dadima (Anar) checks rectal bleeding (Raktastambhana).
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Buttermilk, Surana (elephant foot yam), old rice, warm sitz bath (Avagaha Sweda). Apathya: Straining at stool, prolonged sitting on hard surfaces, spicy chilies, alcohol.
source: Ayurvedic Home Remedies (CCRAS), p. 2 (Ajvain) & p. 3 (Anar); Ashtanga Sangraha Chikitsasthana Ch. 10 (p. 382)
safety_check: Omit black salt in Hypertension; omit sugar in Diabetes

condition_name: Intestinal Worms & Helminthiasis (Krimi Roga)
remedy_name: Karela / Neem Leaf Juice or Dhania-Guda Yoga (with Vidanga)
remedy_text: Option A (Mild/Pediatric): Give 3-5 gm Dhania (coriander) powder with a little jaggery (Guda) twice a day for 5 days. Option B (Adults): Take 10 ml fresh Karela (bitter gourd) juice with a little jaggery on an empty stomach in the morning for 3 days; OR take 20 ml decoction made from a handful of fresh Neem leaves on an empty stomach for 3 days. Classical addition: Vidanga Churna (1-3 gm with honey).
ayurvedic_note: In Ashtanga Sangraha (Chikitsasthana Ch. 22, p. 446), giving a small amount of Guda (jaggery) draws Kaphaja/Purishaja Krimi out of their mucosal hiding places (Utkleshana), while bitter/anthelmintic herbs like Karavellaka (Karela), Nimba, and Vidanga expel and destroy them.
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Bitter vegetables (Karela, Neem, Patola), buttermilk, garlic. Apathya: Excess sweets, jaggery (except as bait with medicine), milk, curd, leafy greens.
source: Ayurvedic Home Remedies (CCRAS), p. 6 (Dhania), p. 14 (Karela), p. 20 (Neem); Ashtanga Sangraha Chikitsasthana Ch. 22 (p. 446)
safety_check: Avoid Karela and Neem internal decoction during Pregnancy and in hypoglycemia

condition_name: Type-2 Diabetes Mellitus & Polyuria (Madhumeha & Prameha)
remedy_name: Nishamalaki (Amla-Haldi Swarasa) & Methi-Karela Seed Yoga
remedy_text: 1) Nishamalaki (Classical First-Line): Mix 10-20 ml fresh Amla juice with 10-20 ml fresh Haldi (turmeric) rhizome juice (or 3 gm each of Amla and Haldi powder) and take twice daily on an empty stomach. 2) Methi / Karela: Take 2 gm Methi (fenugreek) seed powder with milk or warm water twice daily, OR 1-3 gm Karela (bitter gourd) seed powder with water twice a day.
ayurvedic_note: Extolled in Ashtanga Sangraha (Chikitsasthana Ch. 14 Prameha Chikitsa, p. 405: 'Pratah sarvaprameheshu haridram madhuyuktam amalakarasena pibet' — 'In all Pramehas, drink turmeric with Amla juice in the morning!'). Nishamalaki, Methika, and Karavellaka reduce Kleda (tissue dampness) and Meda (adipose), improve insulin sensitivity, and protect against diabetic neuropathy and retinopathy.
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Barley (Yava), old wheat/rice, bitter gourd, fenugreek greens, regular brisk walking (Vyayama). Apathya: Sugar, jaggery, new rice, potato, curd, daytime sleep (Divaswapna), sedentary lifestyle.
source: Ashtanga Sangraha Chikitsasthana Ch. 14 (p. 405); Ayurvedic Home Remedies (CCRAS), p. 4 (Amla), p. 9 (Haldi), p. 14 (Karela), p. 18 (Methi)
safety_check: Monitor blood glucose if taking concurrent allopathic hypoglycemics to prevent hypoglycemia

condition_name: Obesity, Overweight & Dyslipidemia (Sthoulya & Medoroga)
remedy_name: Madhu-Jal (Honey Water) & Triphala-Shilajatu/Guggulu Lekhana Yoga
remedy_text: 1) Daily Home Remedy: Take 1 teaspoon (5 ml) of raw Madhu (honey) stirred in a glass of lukewarm (not boiling) water first thing in the morning on an empty stomach. 2) Classical Support: Take 3-5 gm Triphala Churna with 1 tsp honey and warm water at bedtime or early morning.
ayurvedic_note: In Ashtanga Sangraha (Sutrasthana Ch. 6, p. 43 & Ch. 24 Dvividhopakramaniya, p. 142-143), Madhu (honey) is Guru, Ruksha, Kashaya, and the foremost Lekhana (fat-scraping) substance for Medoroga. Never boil honey or mix it in equal weight with Ghee.
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Barley (Yava), horse gram (Kulattha), old grains, buttermilk, physical exercise (Vyayama). Apathya: Sweet, fried, dairy-heavy foods, daytime sleeping.
source: Ayurvedic Home Remedies (CCRAS), p. 17 (Madhu); Ashtanga Sangraha Sutrasthana Ch. 24 (p. 142-143)
safety_check: Avoid honey in uncontrolled Diabetes and Infants under 1 year

condition_name: Kidney Stones, Burning Micturition & Urinary Tract Infection (Ashmari & Mutrakricchra)
remedy_name: Nariyal Pani (Tender Coconut Water), Gokshura-Punarnava & Kulattha Yusha
remedy_text: 1) Immediate Home Remedy: Drink tender coconut water (Nariyal pani) 2-3 times daily. 2) Classical Decoction: Boil 5 gm Gokshura (Tribulus terrestris) fruits, 5 gm Punarnava root, and 3 gm Dhania seeds in 200 ml water down to 50 ml; drink twice daily. Include horse gram (Kulattha / Gahat dal) soup in diet for kidney stones.
ayurvedic_note: Narikela Jala is Basti-Shodhana (urinary bladder cleanser) and Pittahara (Ashtanga Sangraha Sutrasthana Ch. 6, p. 40). Gokshura is the foremost herb for Mutrakricchra and Ashmari (Ashtanga Sangraha Sutrasthana Ch. 13, p. 98), while Kulattha (Gahat, a staple of Uttarakhand) is Ashmari-bhedana (lithotriptic).
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Plenty of water, tender coconut water, Gahat (Kulattha) dal soup, barley water, ash gourd (Kushmanda). Apathya: Spinach, tomato seeds, excess salt, holding urine urge (Mutra-vegarodha).
source: Ayurvedic Home Remedies (CCRAS), p. 19 (Nariyal); Ashtanga Sangraha Chikitsasthana Ch. 13 (p. 400-402); Madanapala Nighantu Abhayadi Varga
safety_check: Safe across all groups; seek urgent medical evaluation if severe renal colic, fever, or anuria (stopped urine) occurs

condition_name: Iron-Deficiency Anemia, Pallor & Weakness (Pandu Roga)
remedy_name: Amla-Madhu Yoga, Punarnava-Mandura & Dadimadi Ghrita
remedy_text: 1) Daily Home Remedy: Take 10-20 ml fresh Amla juice or 3-5 gm Amla powder with 1 tsp honey or jaggery twice daily, alongside 10 ml Anar (pomegranate) juice and soaked black raisins (Munakka). 2) Classical Formulation (under Vaidya guidance): Punarnava Mandura or Navayasa Loha (250 mg twice daily with buttermilk after meals).
ayurvedic_note: In Ayurvedaprakasha (Ch. 11, p. 154: 'Kittam kashayam shishiram pandushwayathushophajit') and Ashtanga Sangraha (Chikitsasthana Ch. 18, p. 424-425), purified Mandura/Loha combined with Triphala, Trikatu, and Amalaki (rich in Vitamin C) maximizes iron absorption and corrects Rakta-kshaya (anemia).
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Pomegranate, Amla, figs, black raisins, green leafy vegetables cooked with cumin and iron utensils, old rice. Apathya: Excess sour/salty/alkaline foods, clay/soil eating (Mrittika-bhakshana), daytime sleep.
source: Ashtanga Sangraha Chikitsasthana Ch. 18 (p. 424-425); Ayurvedaprakasha Ch. 11 v. 276-277 (p. 154); Ayurvedic Home Remedies (CCRAS), p. 3-4
safety_check: Dietary Amla/Anar/Munakka is safe for all including Pregnancy

condition_name: Sluggish Liver, Mild Jaundice & Biliousness (Kamala & Yakrit Vikara)
remedy_name: Bhumyamalaki-Guduchi-Triphala Kwath & Phalatrikadi Kwath
remedy_text: Prepare 20-30 ml decoction from equal parts of Triphala (Haritaki, Vibhitaki, Amalaki), Guduchi (Giloy), Katuki (Picrorhiza kurroa), Nimba bark, and Bhumyamalaki (Phyllanthus niruri / Bhui Amla). Take twice daily on an empty stomach with 1 tsp honey when cool, alongside fresh sugarcane juice or pomegranate juice.
ayurvedic_note: Described in Ashtanga Sangraha (Chikitsasthana Ch. 18, p. 428: 'Triphalaya guduchya va darvya nimbasya va rasam pratah pratar madhuyutam kamalartaya yojayet') and Chakradatta. Hepatoprotective, choleretic (Pitta-rechaka), and anti-inflammatory.
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Boiled water, sugarcane juice, radish soup, old rice, barley, pomegranate. Apathya: Alcohol, fried/oily food, ghee/fats in acute phase, spicy chilies, non-vegetarian food.
source: Ashtanga Sangraha Chikitsasthana Ch. 18 (p. 428); Chakradatta Pandu-Kamala Chikitsa
safety_check: Note: Scleral icterus / acute jaundice is a Yellow-tier clinical condition requiring liver function test (LFT) at PHC alongside supportive care; avoid Katuki in Pregnancy

condition_name: Joint Pain, Osteoarthritis, Sciatica & Backache (Sandhivata, Kati Shoola & Gridhrasi)
remedy_name: Lahsun (Garlic) Paste & Warm Oil Abhyanga + Methi-Jeera Milk
remedy_text: 1) Oral: Take 5 gm paste of Lahsun (Allium sativum / Garlic) bulb with honey or food twice a day; OR take 2 gm Methi powder mixed with 2 gm Jeera powder in warm milk with a little sugar twice daily. 2) External Massage: Apply warm garlic paste mixed in sesame or mustard oil (or classical Mahanarayana / Bala Taila) over the painful joints.
ayurvedic_note: In Ashtanga Sangraha (Uttarasthana Ch. 49 Rasayana, p. 718: 'Shuddhe va vidhyate vayau na dravyam lashunat param'), Lashuna (garlic) is declared the supreme Vatahara herb for deep-seated bone and joint Vata (Asthi-Majjagata Vata) and Gridhrasi (sciatica).
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Warm water, sesame oil massage, garlic, fenugreek, warm clothing in hill climate. Apathya: Cold water, dry/stale food, chickpeas, exposure to cold winds.
source: Ayurvedic Home Remedies (CCRAS), p. 15 (Lahsun) & p. 18 (Methi); Ashtanga Sangraha Chikitsasthana Ch. 23 & Uttarasthana Ch. 49 (p. 718)
safety_check: Avoid excess internal garlic in Hyperacidity/Peptic Ulcer and bleeding disorders (use Methi-Jeera milk instead)

condition_name: Rheumatoid Arthritis, Joint Swelling & Morning Stiffness (Amavata)
remedy_name: Sonth (Dry Ginger) Decoction with Castor Oil & Valuka Sweda (Dry Sand Fomentation)
remedy_text: 1) Oral: Prepare 10-20 ml decoction from 2 gm dry ginger (Sonth / Nagara) twice daily. In classical Amavata, 5-10 ml Eranda Taila (medical castor oil) is given with warm Sonth decoction at bedtime to clear Ama from the gut and joints. 2) External: Apply dry heat fomentation (Valuka Sweda — warm sand tied in a cloth bolus) over swollen, stiff joints (avoid oil application during acute Ama swelling).
ayurvedic_note: Chakradatta (Amavatachikitsa) and Bhaishajya Ratnavali establish the cardinal rule for Amavata: 'Amavateeshu... langhanam swedanam tiktam dipanam katu bheshajam, virechanam snehapanam bastayashcha marutapahah'. Dry ginger digests Ama while Eranda Taila ('Amavatagajendrasya shariravanacharinah, eka eva nihantasau erandasnehakeshari') acts as a lion destroying the elephant of Amavata.
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Warm water, barley, horse gram, bitter gourd, ginger, dry fomentation. Apathya: Curd, fish, cold water, heavy sweets, oil massage during acute swelling phase.
source: Ayurvedic Home Remedies (CCRAS), p. 1 (Sonth); Chakradatta Amavatachikitsa; Bhaishajya Ratnavali Amavatadhikara
safety_check: Contraindicated in Pregnancy (Eranda Taila) and severe Peptic Ulcer

condition_name: Headache, Tension Headache & Migraine (Shiroroga & Ardhavabhedaka)
remedy_name: Sonth / Dalchini Forehead Lepa (for Cold/Tension Headache) & Amla-Takra Lepa (for Stress/Pitta Headache)
remedy_text: 1) Cold/Sinus/Vata-Kapha Headache: Apply a warm paste of Sonth (dry ginger) powder over the forehead up to 3-4 times a day. 2) Tension Headache: Rub Dalchini (cinnamon) bark with water on a rough stone and apply the paste to the forehead; keep crushed Dalchini pieces near the pillow for soothing aroma. 3) Stress/Pitta Burning Headache: Apply a paste of 25-50 gm Amla fruit rind ground in buttermilk externally over the forehead.
ayurvedic_note: Matches the exact Dosha of the headache: Ushna-Tikshna Lepas (Sunthi, Tvak) relieve Vata-Kapha constriction and sinus heaviness, whereas Sheeta Amla-Takra Lepa (Shirolepa) cools Pitta, relieves mental stress, and promotes sleep (Ashtanga Sangraha Uttarasthana Ch. 28).
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Adequate sleep, foot massage with warm ghee (Padabhyanga), nasal instillation of 2 drops warm cow's ghee or Anu Taila (Pratimarsha Nasya). Apathya: Screen strain, skipping meals, late nights.
source: Ayurvedic Home Remedies (CCRAS), p. 1 (Sonth), p. 4 (Amla), p. 5 (Dalchini); Ashtanga Sangraha Uttarasthana Ch. 28 (p. 604)
safety_check: External applications — 100% safe across all patients

condition_name: Acute Earache without Discharge (Vataja-Kaphaja Karnashoola)
remedy_name: Warm Tulsi / Adrak Swarasa or Laung / Lahsun Siddha Taila Ear Drops (Karnapurana)
remedy_text: Instill 2-3 lukewarm drops of fresh Tulsi leaf juice, OR 2-4 drops of fresh warm Adrak (ginger) juice, OR 2-4 drops of coconut/mustard oil boiled with Lahsun (garlic) paste or Laung (clove) powder into the affected ear twice daily. CRITICAL WARNING: NEVER instill drops if there is pus/fluid discharge (Putikarna) or suspected eardrum perforation!
ayurvedic_note: In Ashtanga Sangraha (Uttarasthana Ch. 22 Karnaroga Pratishedha, p. 578-579), lukewarm Karnapurana with Vatahara Swarasa (Ardraka, Surasa/Tulsi, Lashuna) immediately relieves Vata-Kapha pain in the auditory canal.
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Keeping ears protected from cold wind and water. Apathya: Ear-picking with sharp objects, head bath in cold water.
source: Ayurvedic Home Remedies (CCRAS), p. 1 (Adrak), p. 15 (Lahsun), p. 16 (Laung), p. 25 (Tulsi); Ashtanga Sangraha Uttarasthana Ch. 22 (p. 578-579)
safety_check: STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATED IF EAR DISCHARGE (PUS/FLUID) OR TYMPANIC PERFORATION IS PRESENT

condition_name: Toothache & Dental Caries (Dantashoola & Krimidanta)
remedy_name: Crushed Laung (Clove) or Fried Hing Local Placement
remedy_text: Place a small piece of crushed Laung (Syzygium aromaticum / Clove) or a cotton swab dipped in clove oil, OR a small piece of ghee-fried Hing (Ferula narthex / Asafoetida) directly inside the carious/painful tooth cavity.
ayurvedic_note: Described in Ayurvedic Home Remedies (CCRAS, p. 10 & 16) and Ashtanga Sangraha (Uttarasthana Ch. 26 Mukharoga Pratishedha, p. 596). Eugenol in Lavanga and volatile resins in Hingu provide potent local analgesic, antiseptic, and Vata-pacifying action.
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Warm saline gargles, brushing with astringent twigs/powders. Apathya: Very cold or very hot water, sticky sweets.
source: Ayurvedic Home Remedies (CCRAS), p. 10 (Hing) & p. 16 (Laung); Ashtanga Sangraha Uttarasthana Ch. 26 (p. 596)
safety_check: Local dental application — safe across all patients

condition_name: Bleeding Gums, Gingivitis, Pyorrhoea & Bad Breath (Sheetada, Upakusha & Mukhadaurgandhya)
remedy_name: Tri-Spice Gum Massage (Pratisarana), Amla/Nimbu Massage & Pippali Gargle
remedy_text: 1) Bleeding Gums / Pyorrhoea: Gently massage the gums twice daily after brushing with fine Amla powder, OR crushed Nimbu (lemon) peel, OR a mixture of a pinch of Sonth (ginger), Kalimirach (black pepper), rock salt, honey, and Ghee after gargling with warm salt water. 2) Pippali Gargle: Hold a warm decoction of Pippali mixed with honey and ghee inside the mouth (Gandoosha/Kavala) for a few minutes in the morning and before bedtime. 3) Bad Breath: Chew Saunf (fennel), 1-2 Elaichi seeds, or a small piece of Laung after meals, and gargle with warm Anar rind decoction.
ayurvedic_note: Pratisarana (gentle gingival massage) and Kavala (gargling) remove Kapha-Rakta stagnation in the gums, tighten periodontal tissues (Danta-dardhyakara), and eliminate halitosis (Ashtanga Sangraha Uttarasthana Ch. 26, p. 596-597).
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Regular tongue scraping (Jihva-nirlekhana), warm water gargles, Amla. Apathya: Tobacco/gutkha, sugary sticky foods.
source: Ayurvedic Home Remedies (CCRAS), p. 3, 4, 7, 13, 16, 17, 21, 23, 24; Ashtanga Sangraha Uttarasthana Ch. 26 (p. 596-597)
safety_check: Topical gum massage & gargle — safe for all patients

condition_name: Urticaria, Hives, Prickly Heat & Allergic Skin Rash (Shitapitta, Udarda & Kotha)
remedy_name: AjvainChurna, Haldi-Guda Yoga & Tulsi-Neem Swarasa
remedy_text: Option A: Take 1-2 gm Ajvain (carom seed) powder with water twice daily. Option B: Take 1-3 gm Haldi (turmeric) powder mixed with a little old jaggery (Guda) twice a day. Option C: Take 5-10 ml fresh Tulsi leaf juice twice or thrice daily, OR 10 ml fresh Neem leaf juice with 1 tsp honey twice a day.
ayurvedic_note: Shitapitta and Udarda are caused by cold wind exposure aggravating Vata and Kapha along with Pitta-Rakta (Ashtanga Sangraha Sutrasthana Ch. 20, p. 125). Yavani, Haridra, Tulsi, and Nimba purify Rakta Dhatu and arrest histamine/allergic wheals (Kandu-Kothahara).
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Old rice, Moong dal, bitter gourd, pomegranate, lukewarm water bath with Neem leaves. Apathya: Fish, curd, sour/fermented foods, incompatible food combinations (Viruddha Ahara like milk + fish/salt).
source: Ayurvedic Home Remedies (CCRAS), p. 2 (Ajvain), p. 9 (Haldi), p. 20 (Neem), p. 25 (Tulsi); Chakradatta Shitapitta-Udarda-Kotha Chikitsa
safety_check: Avoid internal Neem in Pregnancy; omit jaggery in Diabetes

condition_name: Fungal Ringworm, Eczema, Scabies & Chronic Skin Diseases (Dadru, Vicharchika & Kushtha)
remedy_name: Neem-Haldi Wash & Lepa + Karela Swarasa + Kalimirach-Nariyal Taila
remedy_text: 1) Topical Wash & Paste: Wash the affected skin with a warm decoction of Neem leaves or Haldi, then apply a paste of fresh Neem leaves or Haldi mixed with Ghee/coconut oil, OR a little Kalimirach powder mixed in coconut oil, OR Tulsi juice mixed with honey and Haldi powder. For scalp/body ringworm, apply a strong decoction of a handful of Neem leaves 1 hour before bath. 2) Internal Blood Purifier: Take 5-10 ml fresh Karela juice on an empty stomach every morning, or 10 ml Neem leaf juice with honey twice daily.
ayurvedic_note: In Ashtanga Sangraha (Chikitsasthana Ch. 21 Kushtha Chikitsa, p. 440-442) and Chakradatta, Nimba and Haridra are premier Kushthaghna and Kandughna (antifungal, antipruritic, and antimicrobial) dravyas.
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Bitter vegetables, old grains, keeping skin dry and clean. Apathya: Curd, jaggery, sesame, urad dal, fish, daytime sleep.
source: Ayurvedic Home Remedies (CCRAS), p. 9 (Haldi), p. 13 (Kalimirach), p. 14 (Karela), p. 20 (Neem), p. 25 (Tulsi); Ashtanga Sangraha Chikitsasthana Ch. 21
safety_check: Topical applications are safe for all; avoid internal Karela/Neem in Pregnancy

condition_name: Acne Vulgaris, Pimples & Facial Hyperpigmentation / Melasma (Yuvanapidika & Vyanga)
remedy_name: Haldi-Anar Seed Lepa, Jayphal-Milk Lepa (for Melasma) & Karela Juice
remedy_text: 1) For Acne / Pimples: Apply a fine paste of Haldi (turmeric) with water/milk, OR a paste of crushed Anar (pomegranate) seeds over the affected part twice daily; also take 5-10 ml fresh Karela juice on an empty stomach once daily. 2) For Black Pigmentation / Melasma (Vyanga, especially around menopausal age): Rub Jayphal (nutmeg) in raw milk to form a smooth paste and apply over pigmented facial areas daily. 3) For Skin Glow: Apply raw Madhu (honey) or Haldi with milk/cream as a face pack.
ayurvedic_note: Described in Ayurvedic Home Remedies (CCRAS, p. 3, 9, 11, 14, 17) and Ashtanga Sangraha (Uttarasthana Ch. 36-37 Kshudraroga Pratishedha, p. 638-641). Jatiphala rubbed in milk clears Vata-Pitta-induced Vyanga (melasma), while Haridra and Dadima clear Kapha-Rakta comedones.
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Adequate water, fresh fruits (Amla, Anar), clean pillowcases. Apathya: Oily/fried junk food, squeezing pimples, night vigil.
source: Ayurvedic Home Remedies (CCRAS), p. 3 (Anar), p. 9 (Haldi), p. 11 (Jayphal), p. 14 (Karela), p. 17 (Madhu); Ashtanga Sangraha Uttarasthana Ch. 37 (p. 640-641)
safety_check: External face packs are 100% safe for all patients

condition_name: Minor Wounds, Cuts, Skin Ulcers & Superficial Burns (Vrana & Dagdha Vrana)
remedy_name: Madhu-Ghrita (Honey & Ghee), Nariyal Taila & Haldi-Neem Antiseptic Dressing
remedy_text: 1) For Superficial Burns & Ulcers: Apply pure cow's Ghee, OR a mixture of Honey and Ghee (in unequal weight), OR pure Nariyal (coconut) oil frequently over the affected area. 2) ForInfected Cuts & Wounds: Wash the wound with a cooled decoction of Haldi or Neem leaves, then apply a warm paste of fresh Neem leaves, OR Haldi paste mixed with Ghee/coconut oil, OR Tulsi juice mixed with honey and Haldi powder.
ayurvedic_note: In Ashtanga Sangraha (Sutrasthana Ch. 40 Agnikarma, p. 210 & Uttarasthana Ch. 30-31 Vrana Pratishedha, p. 614-620), Madhu-Sarpi (honey and ghee) and Haridra-Nimba are the primary Vrana-Shodhana (wound-cleansing) and Vrana-Ropana (granulation-promoting) agents.
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Old rice, Moong dal, pointed gourd (Patola), pomegranate. Apathya: Curd, sour/fermented foods, daytime sleep (which increases pus/Kleda in wounds).
source: Ayurvedic Home Remedies (CCRAS), p. 8 (Ghee), p. 9 (Haldi), p. 17 (Madhu), p. 19 (Nariyal), p. 20 (Neem), p. 25 (Tulsi); Ashtanga Sangraha Uttarasthana Ch. 30
safety_check: For minor superficial wounds/burns only; deep, bleeding, or animal-bite wounds require immediate PHC tetanus & surgical care

condition_name: Hair Fall, Premature Greying & Dandruff (Khalitya, Palitya & Darunaka)
remedy_name: Amla-Methi-Tulsi Siddha Nariyal Taila & Neem Scalp Wash
remedy_text: 1) Daily Hair Oil: Regularly massage the scalp with Coconut oil (Nariyal taila) processed/boiled with Methi powder and Amla powder (or dried Nimbu skin powder, or Tulsi juice). 2) Pre-Bath Scalp Pack: Soak Amla fruit rind overnight in water and apply the water/paste to the scalp 2 hours before bath; OR massage scalp with Methi seed paste mixed in water 1/2 hour before bath (excellent natural hair conditioner); OR wash scalp with Neem leaf decoction 1 hour before bath for dandruff. 3) Internal Rasayana: Eat 1-2 fresh Amla fruits every morning to prevent hair fall and premature greying.
ayurvedic_note: Amalaki is Vayahsthapana (anti-aging) and Keshya (hair tonic) par excellence (Ashtanga Sangraha Sutrasthana Ch. 13, p. 99 & Uttarasthana Ch. 28 Shiroroga Pratishedha, p. 607-609). Methika and Nimba clear Kapha-Vata scaling (Darunaka/dandruff).
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Amla, curry leaves, black sesame seeds, adequate sleep, nasal instillation of 2 drops Anu Taila. Apathya: Washing hair with very hot water, excessive salt/sour/spicy intake, mental stress.
source: Ayurvedic Home Remedies (CCRAS), p. 4 (Amla), p. 18 (Methi), p. 19 (Nariyal), p. 20 (Neem), p. 21 (Nimbu), p. 25 (Tulsi); Ashtanga Sangraha Uttarasthana Ch. 28 (p. 607-609)
safety_check: 100% Safe for all age groups

condition_name: Painful Menstruation & Dysmenorrhea (Kashtartava & Udavartini Yonivyapad)
remedy_name: Ajvain-Warm Milk Yoga &Hing-Ghee Anulomana
remedy_text: Take 1-2 gm powder of Ajvain (Trachyspermum ammi) seeds with warm milk thrice a day for 2-3 days during painful menses. Apply a warm water bag or warm sesame oil over the lower abdomen (pelvis).
ayurvedic_note: In Ashtanga Sangraha (Sharirasthana Ch. 1, p. 214 & Uttarasthana Ch. 38-39 Guhyaroga Pratishedha, p. 644-648), painful menstruation is caused by upward/obstructed Apana Vata ('Na hi vatadrite yonir vanitanam prarohati'). Yavani (Ajvain) with warm milk is Ushna, Vata-anulomaka, and antispasmodic.
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Warm milk, sesame, jaggery, rest, warm abdominal fomentation. Apathya: Cold drinks, raw salads, heavy physical exertion during menses.
source: Ayurvedic Home Remedies (CCRAS), p. 2 (Ajvain); Ashtanga Sangraha Uttarasthana Ch. 39 (p. 647-648)
safety_check: Contraindicated in Pregnancy and heavy menorrhagia (Asrigdara)

condition_name: Postpartum Lactation Deficiency (Stanyakshaya)
remedy_name: Methi Churna with Warm Milk & Shatavari Kalpa (Galactagogue)
remedy_text: Take 5 gm Methi (Trigonella foenum-graecum / Fenugreek) seed powder with warm milk and a little sugar every morning. Classical addition: Take 3-5 gm Shatavari (Asparagus racemosus) root powder with warm milk twice daily.
ayurvedic_note: Methika and Shatavari nourish Rasa Dhatu and Upadhatu Stanya (breast milk) while pacifying postpartum Vata (Sutika Vata) as described in Ashtanga Sangraha (Sutrasthana Ch. 15 Mahakashaya — Stanyajanana Gana, p. 104).
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Warm milk, ghee, moong dal, garlic, fenugreek ladoo, adequate hydration and rest. Apathya: Dry, spicy, astringent foods, stress/grief.
source: Ayurvedic Home Remedies (CCRAS), p. 18 (Methi); Ashtanga Sangraha Sutrasthana Ch. 15 (p. 104)
safety_check: Safe for lactating mothers; omit sugar if gestational/postpartum diabetes is present

condition_name: Mental Stress, Anxiety, Restlessness & Memory Enhancement (Manodvega, Anidra & Smritikshaya)
remedy_name: Amla-Takra Shirolepa, Dalchini Aroma, Jayphal-Milk & Daily Cow's Ghee
remedy_text: 1) For Adult Mental Stress & Insomnia: Apply a paste of 25-50 gm Amla rind ground in buttermilk externally over the forehead (Shirolepa); keep crushed Dalchini pieces in a handkerchief or near the pillow for its soothing aroma. 2) For Memory & Brain Development in Children: Give 1 tsp pure cow's Ghee daily in warm milk or food. 3) For Pediatric Restlessness & Irritability: Give 1-2 pinches (~125 mg) of Jayphal (nutmeg) powder with warm milk at bedtime as a mild natural sedative.
ayurvedic_note: In Ashtanga Sangraha (Sutrasthana Ch. 6, p. 41: 'Shastam dhismritimedhagnibalayuhshukrachakshusham... snehanam uttamamitam vayasah sthapanam param'), cow's Ghrita is the supreme Medhya (intellect/memory enhancer) and Vata-Pitta pacifier.
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Meditation, yoga, regular sleep, warm milk with ghee, Brahmi/Mandukaparni. Apathya: Excess tea/coffee, late-night screen exposure, tobacco/alcohol.
source: Ayurvedic Home Remedies (CCRAS), p. iii, p. 4 (Amla), p. 5 (Dalchini), p. 8 (Ghee), p. 11 (Jayphal); Ashtanga Sangraha Sutrasthana Ch. 6 (p. 41) & Uttarasthana Ch. 49 (p. 708)
safety_check: 100% Safe across all patients

condition_name: General Debility, Convalescence & Immunity Boosting (Daurbalya & Ojakshaya)
remedy_name: Amalaki Rasayana / Chyavanaprasha Avaleha (Classical Rejuvenative)
remedy_text: 1) Daily Home Rasayana: Take 1-2 fresh Amla fruits or 3-5 gm Amla powder with milk/honey daily. 2) Classical Chyavanaprasha Avaleha (prepared from 500 Amla fruits cooked in Dashamoola-Jeevaniya decoction with Ghee, Sesame oil, Honey, Pippali, Vamshalochana, and Trijata): Take 10-12 gm (1 tbsp) every morning on an empty stomach followed by warm milk.
ayurvedic_note: Detailed in Ashtanga Sangraha (Uttarasthana Ch. 49 Rasayana Vidhi, p. 705-706): Chyavanaprasha restores Ojas, strengthens Pranavaha Srotas (lungs/immunity), kindles Agni, and relieves chronic cough, dyspnea, hoarseness, and post-illness weakness in children, adults, and the elderly alike.
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Milk, ghee, wholesome Sattvika diet, regular routine (Dinacharya). Apathya: Stale, processed, or incompatible foods.
source: Ashtanga Sangraha Uttarasthana Ch. 49 (p. 705-706); Ayurvedic Home Remedies (CCRAS), p. 4 (Amla)
safety_check: Use sugar-free Amla Churna instead of Chyavanaprasha in uncontrolled Diabetes; avoid honey in infants <1 year

condition_name: Eye Strain, Burning Eyes & Conjunctival Irritation (Netra Daha & Abhishyanda)
remedy_name: Triphala Eye Wash (Netra Prakshalana) & Oral Triphala-Ghrita-Madhu
remedy_text: 1) Oral Chakshushya Yoga: Take 3 gm Triphala Churna mixed with 1/2 tsp Ghee and 1 tsp Honey (unequal weight) at bedtime. 2) External Eye Wash: Soak 1 tsp Triphala powder in a glass of boiled and cooled water overnight, filter 3 times through a sterile/clean fine muslin cloth in the morning, and splash/wash the eyes gently.
ayurvedic_note: In Ashtanga Sangraha (Sutrasthana Ch. 13 Agryasangraha, p. 98: 'Triphala timiraghnanam' & Uttarasthana Ch. 16 Timira Pratishedha, p. 558), Triphala with Ghee and Honey is the supreme Chakshushya (vision-protecting) formulation.
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Padabhyanga (foot massage with ghee), green gram, Amla, pomegranate. Apathya: Prolonged screen glare, rubbing eyes, daytime sleep.
source: Ashtanga Sangraha Sutrasthana Ch. 13 (p. 98) & Uttarasthana Ch. 16 (p. 558); Chakradatta Netrarogachikitsa
safety_check: Ensure eye wash water is boiled, cooled, and triple-filtered; avoid oral Triphala in Pregnancy

condition_name: Anorexia & Tastelessness (Aruchi & Bhaktadwesha)
remedy_name: Dalchini-Ajvain Chewable Churna
remedy_text: Mix equal parts of Dalchini (cinnamon) bark powder and Ajvain (carom seed) powder. Take 2 gm in three divided doses for slow chewing before food.
ayurvedic_note: Clears Kapha coating on the taste buds (Bodhaka Kapha) and stimulates salivary and gastric secretions.
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Warm water, pomegranate, lemon. Apathya: Heavy, cold, sweet foods.
source: Ayurvedic Home Remedies (CCRAS), p. 5 (Dalchini)
safety_check: Safe for all adult patients

condition_name: Loss of Appetite & Sluggish Digestion (Agnimandya)
remedy_name: Nimbu-Kalimirach Pre-Meal Appetizer
remedy_text: Take 5-10 ml (2 teaspoons) of fresh Nimbu (lemon) juice with a pinch of black pepper (Kalimirach) powder and rock salt in a little water 30 minutes before meals.
ayurvedic_note: Amla Rasa of Nimbu combined with Katu Rasa of Maricha kindles Jatharagni and clears Kapha-Vata stagnation in the stomach.
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Light freshly cooked meals. Apathya: Overeating, cold water.
source: Ayurvedic Home Remedies (CCRAS), p. 13 (Kalimirach) & p. 21 (Nimbu)
safety_check: Avoid black pepper in active Peptic Ulcer

condition_name: Loss of Appetite with Pitta/WormTendency (Kaphapitta Aruchi)
remedy_name: Karela-Takra Yoga or Neem Leaf Decoction
remedy_text: Option A: Take 5-10 ml fresh Karela (bitter gourd) juice mixed with buttermilk 1-2 times daily. Option B: Take 20 ml decoction made from a handful of fresh Neem leaves on an empty stomach for 3 days.
ayurvedic_note: Tikta Rasa (bitter taste) of Karavellaka and Nimba is inherently Aruchighna (relieves tastelessness), Deepana, andPachana (Ashtanga Sangraha Sutrasthana Ch. 18, p. 114: 'Tiktah swayam aruchishnuh aruchim hanti').
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Buttermilk, light diet. Apathya: Sweets, heavy fried food.
source: Ayurvedic Home Remedies (CCRAS), p. 14 (Karela) & p. 20 (Neem); Ashtanga Sangraha Sutrasthana Ch. 18 (p. 114)
safety_check: Contraindicated in Pregnancy

condition_name: Chronic Indigestion & Mucus Accumulation (Kaphaja Agnimandya)
remedy_name: Pippali-Guda Yoga & Madhu-Maricha Linctus
remedy_text: Option A: Take 2 gm Pippali (long pepper) powder mixed with equal quantity of old Jaggery (Guda) twice daily before meals. Option B: Take 1 tsp Honey (Madhu) with a pinch of black pepper (Kalimirach) powder 3-4 times a day.
ayurvedic_note: Pippali with Guda digests chronic Ama and strengthens the digestive fire without causing Vata dryness.
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Warm water, light diet. Apathya: Cold drinks, heavy sweets.
source: Ayurvedic Home Remedies (CCRAS), p. 17 (Madhu) & p. 23 (Pippali); Chakradatta Agnimandyachikitsa
safety_check: Contraindicated in Peptic Ulcer, Pregnancy (high dose Pippali), and Diabetes (Guda/Madhu)

condition_name: Indigestion with Gas & Bloating (Vataja Ajirna)
remedy_name: Laung Churna or Dalchini Churna with Warm Water
remedy_text: Take 1-2 gm Laung (clove) powder OR 2 gm Dalchini (cinnamon) bark powder with warm water twice daily after meals.
ayurvedic_note: Lavanga and Tvak are Deepana, Pachana, and Shoolaprashamana, relieving Vata-type indigestion (Vishtabdha Ajirna) characterized by bloating and colic.
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Warm water, light warm soup. Apathya: Cold, dry, gas-forming foods.
source: Ayurvedic Home Remedies (CCRAS), p. 5 (Dalchini) & p. 16 (Laung)
safety_check: Safe across general adult populations

condition_name: Acute Fever with Body Ache & Chills (Vataja / Vata-Kapha Jwara)
remedy_name: Kiratadi Kwath & Dashamoola Kwath
remedy_text: Prepare 20-30 ml decoction from equal parts of Kiratatikta (Swertia chirata), Musta, Guduchi (Giloy), Shunthi (dry ginger), Shalaparni, Prishniparni, Brihati, Kantakari, and Gokshura. Take warm twice daily.
ayurvedic_note: Described in Bhaishajya Ratnavali (Jwaradhikara v. 69-70, p. 32-33). Pacifies Vataja Jwara characterized by shivering, body ache (Angamarda), headache, and fluctuating temperature.
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Warm gruel (Laja Peya), warm water. Apathya: Cold air, daytime sleep, heavy food.
source: Bhaishajya Ratnavali Jwaradhikara v. 69-70 (p. 32-33); Ashtanga Sangraha Chikitsasthana Ch. 1
safety_check: Safe across adult populations

condition_name: High Fever with Burning Eyes, Delirium & Thirst (Pittaja Jwara)
remedy_name: Parpatadi Kwath & Dhanya-Sharkara Hima
remedy_text: 1) Parpatadi Kwath: Prepare 20 ml decoction from Parpataka (Fumaria indica), Raktachandana, Ushira (Khus), and Musta; take cooled with 1 tsp sugar/misri twice daily. 2) Dhanya-Sharkara Yoga: Soak 10 gm crushed Dhania (coriander seeds) in 150 ml water overnight; filter in the morning, add 1 tsp sugar/misri, and drink on an empty stomach.
ayurvedic_note: From Bhaishajya Ratnavali (Jwaradhikara v. 73-74, p. 34). Dhanya-Sharkara cold infusion rapidly extinguishes internal burning (Antardaha), bilious vomiting, and Pittaja fever.
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Cool shade, parched rice gruel with sugar, pomegranate. Apathya: Hot, spicy, sour, salty foods, sun exposure.
source: Bhaishajya Ratnavali Jwaradhikara v. 73-74 (p. 34); Ashtanga Sangraha Chikitsasthana Ch. 1
safety_check: Omit sugar in Diabetes; 100% safe in Gastritis and Pregnancy

condition_name: Fever with Cough, Heaviness, Coryza & Drowsiness (Kaphaja Jwara)
remedy_name: Nimbadi Kwath &Sindhuvaradi Kwath
remedy_text: Prepare 20-30 ml decoction from Nimba bark, Shunthi (dry ginger), Guduchi (Giloy), Devadaru, Shati, Kiratatikta, Pushkaramoola, Brihati, Kantakari, and Pippali; OR decoction of Sindhuvara (Nirgundi) leaves with a pinch of Pippali powder. Take warm twice daily.
ayurvedic_note: From Bhaishajya Ratnavali (Jwaradhikara v. 79-81, p. 35-36). Dries excess Kapha, opens blocked respiratory channels, and resolves Kaphaja Jwara.
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Langhana (fasting/light soup), warm water. Apathya: Milk, ghee, sweets, daytime sleep.
source: Bhaishajya Ratnavali Jwaradhikara v. 79-81 (p. 35-36)
safety_check: Avoid in Pregnancy and severe Peptic Ulcer

condition_name: Fever with Diarrhoea / Gastroenteritis (Jwaratisara)
remedy_name: Ushiradi Kwath / Nagaradi Kwath (Classical Jwaratisara Decoction)
remedy_text: Prepare 20-30 ml decoction from equal parts of Ushira (Khus), Balaka (Hrivera), Musta, Dhanyaka (Coriander), Shunthi (Dry ginger), Dhataki flowers, Lodhra, and unripe Bilva pulp. Take twice daily.
ayurvedic_note: In Bhaishajya Ratnavali (Jwaratisaradhikara v. 1-8, p. 257-259), ordinary fever medicines may worsen diarrhea and ordinary anti-diarrheal astringents may trap fever; Ushiradi and Nagaradi Kwathas digest Ama and simultaneously resolve both Jwara and Atisara.
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Laja Manda, thin rice gruel cooked with Bilva and Shunthi, boiled water. Apathya: Heavy solid food, milk, cold water.
source: Bhaishajya Ratnavali Jwaratisaradhikara v. 5-8 (p. 259); Chakradatta Jwaratisarachikitsa
safety_check: Safe across adult populations; monitor hydration status closely

condition_name: Acute Diarrhoea with Indigestion, Mucus & Abdominal Cramping (Ama Atisara)
remedy_name: Dhanyapanchaka Kwath (Classical Five-Herb Ama-Digesting Decoction)
remedy_text: Prepare 20-30 ml decoction from equal parts of Dhanyaka (Coriander), Nagara/Sunthi (Dry ginger), Musta (Nutgrass), Balaka (Hrivera), and unripe Bilva pulp (omit Sunthi if Pittatisara / burning stool is present). Take warm twice or thrice daily.
ayurvedic_note: From Bhaishajya Ratnavali (Atisaradhikara v. 30-31, p. 279) and Chakradatta (Atisarachikitsa, p. 29). In Ama Atisara (sticky, foul-smelling stools with cramps), stopping stools prematurely causes complications; Dhanyapanchaka digests Ama (Amapachana), relieves pain (Shoolaghna), and naturally normalizes stool consistency.
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Thin rice gruel (Yavagu/Peya), buttermilk. Apathya: Heavy foods, milk, wheat.
source: Bhaishajya Ratnavali Atisaradhikara v. 30-31 (p. 279); Chakradatta Atisarachikitsa (p. 29)
safety_check: Omit Sunthi in Pittatisara / bloody stools (becomes Dhanyachatushka)

condition_name: Chronic Diarrhoea, Malabsorption Syndrome & IBS (Grahani Doshaja Atisara)
remedy_name: Gangadhara Churna & Dadimashtaka Churna
remedy_text: 1) Laghu Gangadhara Churna: Equal parts of Musta, Indrayava, Bilva pulp, Lodhra, Mocharasa, and Dhataki flowers; take 3 gm with buttermilk or rice water (Tandulodaka) and honey twice daily. 2) Dadimashtaka Churna: Prepared from Dadima (pomegranate), Tvak, Ela, Patra, Nagakesara, Ajmoda, Dhanyaka, Jeeraka, Trikatu, and Sharkara; take 3-5 gm with buttermilk after meals.
ayurvedic_note: From Bhaishajya Ratnavali (Grahanyadhikara v. 44-47, p. 311) and Ashtanga Sangraha (Chikitsasthana Ch. 11, p. 394-395). Restores the Agni of the Grahani (duodenum/small intestine) and checks chronic loose motions.
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Buttermilk (Takra), old rice, pomegranate, roasted cumin. Apathya: Milk, leafy greens, heavy pulses.
source: Ashtanga Sangraha Chikitsasthana Ch. 11 (p. 394-395); Bhaishajya Ratnavali Grahanyadhikara v. 44-47 (p. 311); Chakradatta (p. 39)
safety_check: Omit sugar in Dadimashtaka if diabetic (use Gangadhara Churna instead)

condition_name: Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS-D) with Alternating Loose Stools & Mucus (Grahani)
remedy_name: Chitrakadi Gutika (Classical Agni-Kindling Tablet)
remedy_text: Prepared from Chitraka root, Pippali moola, Yavakshara, Sajjikshara, five Lavanas, Trikatu, Hingu, and Ajmoda triturated in lemon/pomegranate juice. Take 1-2 tablets (250-500 mg) with warm water or buttermilk after meals twice daily.
ayurvedic_note: Described in Bhaishajya Ratnavali (Grahanyadhikara v. 30-33, p. 308) and Chakradatta (p. 39). Digesting Ama and rekindling Mandagni in the Grahani is the root cure for chronic mucus colitis and IBS.
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Buttermilk, light warm meals. Apathya: Raw salads, cold drinks, curd, heavy fried food.
source: Bhaishajya Ratnavali Grahanyadhikara v. 30-33 (p. 308); Chakradatta Grahanychikitsa (p. 39)
safety_check: Contraindicated in Pregnancy, Hyperacidity/Peptic Ulcer, and Hypertension

condition_name: Generalized Body Ache, Myalgia & Fatigue (Angamarda & Shrama)
remedy_name: Sonth Kwath OR Methi-Jeera Warm Milk
remedy_text: Option A: Prepare 10-20 ml decoction from 2 gm dry ginger (Sonth) and take warm twice daily. Option B (Gentle/Nourishing): Mix 2 gm Methi (fenugreek) powder with 2 gm Jeera (cumin) powder in a cup of warm milk with a little sugar and drink twice daily.
ayurvedic_note: Methika and Jiraka with warm milk nourish depleted Dhatus and calm Vata-induced myalgia (Angamarda), while Sunthi decoction relieves Kapha-Ama muscular stiffness.
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Warm water bath, gentle oil massage (Abhyanga), adequate rest. Apathya: Cold exposure, overexertion.
source: Ayurvedic Home Remedies (CCRAS), p. 1 (Adrak/Sonth) & p. 18 (Methi)
safety_check: Methi-Jeera milk is safe in Gastritis; avoid Sonth in severe Peptic Ulcer

condition_name: Severe Bronchial Cough, Asthma & Chest Pain (Kasa, Shwasa & Parshvashoola)
remedy_name: Kantakaryavaleha & Dashamoola Kwath
remedy_text: 1) Kantakaryavaleha: Herbal linctus prepared from Kantakari (Solanum xanthocarpum) decoction cooked with Guduchi, Chavya, Chitraka, Musta, Karkatashringi, Trikatu, Bharangi, Rasna, Ghee, Sugar, Honey, and Vamshalochana. Take 5-10 gm twice daily with warm water/milk. 2) Dashamoola Kwath: 20-30 ml warm decoction with a pinch of Pippali powder twice daily.
ayurvedic_note: In Ashtanga Sangraha (Sutrasthana Ch. 13 Agryasangraha, p. 97: 'Kantakarika kasaghnanam') and Chikitsasthana Ch. 4 (p. 346-347), Kantakari is the foremost herb for Kasa, Hikka, and Shwasa, acting as a potent bronchodilator and mucolytic.
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Warm water, horse gram soup, light warm food. Apathya: Cold air, curd, refrigerated foods.
source: Ashtanga Sangraha Sutrasthana Ch. 13 (p. 97) & Chikitsasthana Ch. 4 (p. 346-347); Chakradatta Kasachikitsa
safety_check: Omit sugar-based Avaleha in uncontrolled Diabetes (use Dashamoola-Kantakari Kwath instead)

condition_name: Chronic Cough, Allergic Bronchitis & Post-Viral Weakness (Kshataja/Kshayaja Kasa)
remedy_name: Agastya Haritaki Rasayana (Classical Respiratory Rejuvenative)
remedy_text: Classical Avaleha prepared from Haritaki fruits cooked in Dashamoola, Chitraka, Shati, Bala, Apamarga, Shankhapushpi, Bharangi, and Pushkaramoola decoction with Yava (barley), Ghee, Til Taila, Guda, Pippali, and Honey. Take 5-10 gm twice daily with warm milk or water.
ayurvedic_note: Extolled in Ashtanga Sangraha (Chikitsasthana Ch. 5 Kshatakshaya Kasa Chikitsa, p. 352) as the supreme Rasayana for eliminating all 5 types of Kasa, Shwasa, Hikka, Vishama Jwara, Peenasa (chronic sinusitis), and Grahani while rejuvenating strength.
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Warm milk, wholesome nourishing diet. Apathya: Cold, dry, pungent foods, smoking.
source: Ashtanga Sangraha Chikitsasthana Ch. 5 (p. 352); Chakradatta Kasachikitsa
safety_check: Contraindicated in Pregnancy (contains Haritaki) and uncontrolled Diabetes

condition_name: Acid Peptic Disease, Gastritis & Epigastric Burning (Amlapitta & Pittaja Shoola)
remedy_name: Dhania-Saunf-Misri Hima (Cold Coriander-Fennel Infusion) & Patoladi Kwath
remedy_text: 1) Home Cold Infusion (Hima): Soak 5 gm crushed Dhania (coriander) seeds and 5 gm Saunf (fennel) seeds in 150 ml room-temperature water for 2-4 hours (or overnight); macerate, strain, add 1 tsp Misri (rock sugar), and drink twice daily. 2) Classical Kwath: Patoladi Kwath (Patola leaves, Guduchi, Nimba, Parpataka, Amalaki) 20 ml twice daily.
ayurvedic_note: Hima Kalpana (cold infusion) preserves cooling volatile principles that soothe gastric mucosal inflammation (Pittashamana) without suppressing digestive Agni.
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Pomegranate, coconut water, cold milk, barley, pointed gourd (Parwal/Patola). Apathya: Chili, pickles, garlic, tea/coffee, fasting.
source: Ayurvedic Home Remedies (CCRAS), p. 6 (Dhania) & p. 24 (Saunf); Ashtanga Sangraha Chikitsasthana Ch. 1
safety_check: 100% Safe in Pregnancy, Hypertension, and Peptic Ulcer; omit Misri in Diabetes

condition_name: Severe Gastric Hyperacidity, Duodenal Ulcer & Colicky Epigastric Pain (Parinama Shoola)
remedy_name: Shankha Bhasma / Kapardika Bhasma with Amla & Honey-Ghee
remedy_text: Under Ayurvedic supervision: Take 250 mg purified Shankha Bhasma (conch shell calx) mixed with 2 gm Amla powder and 1/2 tsp Ghee twice daily before meals, or with Nimbu Swarasa.
ayurvedic_note: In Ayurvedaprakasha (Ch. 8 v. 17-20, p. 109: 'Shankhah ksharo himo grahi grahanirorganashanah, parinamashoolanut') and Bhaishajya Ratnavali, Shankha Bhasma is Sheeta (cooling), Kshariya (antacid), Grahi, and specifically cures Parinama Shoola (peptic ulcer pain occurring during digestion) and Grahani.
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Milk, ghee, old rice, coconut water. Apathya: Spicy, sour, fried foods, NSAIDs/alcohol.
source: Ayurvedaprakasha Ch. 8 v. 17-20 (p. 109) & Ch. 10 v. 8-9 (p. 114)
safety_check: Use only properly Shodhita and Marita Bhasma; safe in Gastritis and Ulcer

condition_name: Pedal Edema, Fluid Retention, Puffiness & Sluggish Kidney/Liver Function (Shotha / Shwayathu)
remedy_name: Punarnavashtaka Kwath & Ardraka-Guda Yoga
remedy_text: 1) Punarnavashtaka Kwath: Prepare 20-30 ml decoction from equal parts of Punarnava (Boerhavia diffusa), Nimba, Patola, Shunthi, Katuki, Guduchi, Devadaru, and Haritaki; take twice daily. 2) Ardraka-Guda Yoga: Take equal parts of fresh crushed ginger (Adrak) and old Jaggery (Guda) starting from 5 gm daily, gradually increasing as per digestive power with milk/light diet.
ayurvedic_note: Described in Ashtanga Sangraha (Chikitsasthana Ch. 19 Shwayathu Chikitsa, p. 429) and Chakradatta. Punarnava is the premier Mutrala (diuretic) and Shothahara (anti-edematous) herb, clearing Kleda without depleting potassium or vitality.
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Barley, old rice, buttermilk, Punarnava greens, salt-restricted diet. Apathya: Excess salt (Lavana), curd, heavy/fried foods, daytime sleep.
source: Ashtanga Sangraha Chikitsasthana Ch. 19 (p. 429); Chakradatta Shothachikitsa
safety_check: Note: Generalized edema or facial/pedal swelling in pregnancy requires immediate PHC blood pressure & renal check; omit Guda in Diabetes

condition_name: Epistaxis (Nosebleed), Heavy Menstrual Bleeding & Heat-Induced Bleeding (Raktapitta & Asrigdara)
remedy_name: Anar Swarasa, Vasa Swarasa with Misri & Durva/Amalaki Cooling Yoga
remedy_text: 1) Immediate Home Care: Take 10-20 ml fresh sweet Anar (pomegranate) juice or Amla juice with 1 tsp Misri (rock candy) twice daily; drink tender coconut water. For nosebleed, instill 2 drops of fresh Durva (Cynodon dactylon) grass juice or pomegranate flower juice or cold milk into the nostrils and apply a cold paste of Amla/Sandalwood on the forehead. 2) Classical (Non-Pregnant): 10 ml fresh Vasa (Adusa) leaf juice with 1 tsp sugar and honey twice daily.
ayurvedic_note: In Ashtanga Sangraha (Chikitsasthana Ch. 3 Raktapitta Chikitsa, p. 339: 'Vrishah sadyo jayatyasram sa hi tasya paramaushadham'), Vasa, Dadima, Amalaki, and Ushira cool aggravated Pitta in Rakta Dhatu and arrest capillary bleeding (Raktastambhana).
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Cool milk, pomegranate, Amla, Moong soup, rest in a cool room. Apathya: Hot sun, spicy/sour/salty/fermented foods, garlic, hing, anger, physical exertion.
source: Ashtanga Sangraha Chikitsasthana Ch. 3 (p. 338-341); Chakradatta Raktapitta Chikitsa (p. 86); Ayurvedic Home Remedies (CCRAS), p. 3-4
safety_check: Avoid Vasa in Pregnancy (use Anar, Amla, and Durva instead); seek urgent PHC care if bleeding is profuse

condition_name: Gout, Hyperuricemia & Burning/Swollen Small Joints (Vatarakta / Vatashonita)
remedy_name: Guduchi Kwath (Giloy Decoction) & Kaishora Guggulu
remedy_text: 1) Daily Decoction: Prepare 20-30 ml decoction (or 10 ml fresh stem juice) of Guduchi (Tinospora cordifolia / Giloy) and take twice daily. 2) Classical: Kaishora Guggulu (prepared from Guduchi, Triphala, and purified Guggulu) 1-2 tablets twice daily with Guduchi Kwath after meals. Apply cooling Shatadhauta Ghrita or Guduchi-milk paste externally over burning/red joints.
ayurvedic_note: In Ashtanga Sangraha (Sutrasthana Ch. 13 Agryasangraha, p. 98: 'Amrita sangrahaniyadipaniyavatashleshmashonitavibandhaprashamananam' & Chikitsasthana Ch. 24 Vatashonita Chikitsa, p. 456-457), Amrita (Guduchi) is the undisputed #1 specific herb for Vatarakta (gout/inflammatory arthritis involving Rakta and Vata).
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Old rice, barley, pointed gourd (Patola), milk, Amla, Giloy. Apathya: Urad dal, horse gram (Kulattha), red meat, alcohol, sour curd, radish, daytime sleep.
source: Ashtanga Sangraha Sutrasthana Ch. 13 (p. 98) & Chikitsasthana Ch. 24 (p. 456-457); Bhaishajya Ratnavali Vataraktadhikara
safety_check: Guduchi Kwath is safe for all; avoid Guggulu in Pregnancy

condition_name: Mild Palpitations, Heat-Induced Restlessness & Cardiac Tonic Support (Hridroga - Non-Emergency)
remedy_name: Arjuna Ksheerapaka (Terminalia arjuna Bark Milk Decoction) & Amla-Anar
remedy_text: Boil 3-5 gm coarse powder of Arjuna (Terminalia arjuna) bark in 100 ml milk and 400 ml water on low heat until the water evaporates and 100 ml milk remains (Ksheerapaka). Strain and drink warm once or twice daily. Also include fresh Anar (pomegranate) and Amla regularly in the diet.
ayurvedic_note: In Ashtanga Sangraha (Chikitsasthana Ch. 8 Hridroga Chikitsa, p. 369) and Chakradatta, Arjuna bark cooked in milk (Ksheerapaka) and Dadima (Anar) are Hridya (cardioprotective), strengthening cardiac muscle (Mamsa-Rakta Dhatu) and calming Vyana-Prana Vata and Sadhaka Pitta.
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Old rice, Moong soup, pomegranate, Amla, calm mind. Apathya: Excess salt, oily/fried food, anger, strenuous exertion.
source: Ashtanga Sangraha Chikitsasthana Ch. 8 (p. 368-369); Chakradatta Hridrogachikitsa; Ayurvedic Home Remedies (CCRAS), p. 3-4
safety_check: NOTE: Acute chest pain, pressure, sweating, or breathlessness is a RED-TIER EMERGENCY requiring immediate 108/hospital referral! Use Arjuna Ksheerapaka only for chronic supportive care.

condition_name: Leucorrhoea / White Vaginal Discharge & Pelvic Weakness (Shweta Pradara)
remedy_name: Amalaki Churna with Honey/Misri & Pushyanuga Churna with Tandulodaka
remedy_text: 1) Home Remedy: Take 3-5 gm Amla (Amalaki) seed/fruit powder mixed with honey and sugar/misri, or washed rice water (Tandulodaka) twice daily. 2) Classical Formulation: Pushyanuga Churna (Patha, Jambu seed, Amra seed, Pashanabheda, Rasanjana, Ambashtha, Mocharasa, Samanga, Padmakesara, Vahlika, Ativisha, Musta, Bilva, Lodhra, Gairika, Katphala, Maricha, Shunthi, मृद्वीका, Raktachandana, Kutaja, Sariva, Dhataki, Madhuka, Arjuna) 3 gm with 1 tsp honey followed by Tandulodaka (rice-wash water) twice daily.
ayurvedic_note: Extolled in Ashtanga Sangraha (Uttarasthana Ch. 39 Guhyaroga Pratishedha, p. 650-651: 'Churnam pushyanugam nama hitam atreyapujitam...madhuna'). It is Kashaya-Stambhana, Kapha-Pitta shamaka, and heals cervical/vaginal mucosal discharge.
pathya_apathya: Pathya: Rice water (Tandulodaka), Amla, pomegranate, personal hygiene (Triphala/Panchavalkala wash). Apathya: Spicy, sour, fermented foods, curd, excess coitus.
source: Ashtanga Sangraha Uttarasthana Ch. 39 (p. 650-651); Chakradatta Asrigdarachikitsa
safety_check: Safe for adult women; omit honey in infants

condition_name: Pediatric Cough, Fever, Vomiting & Diarrhoea (Bala Roga — Kasa, Jwara, Chhardi, Atisara)
remedy_name: Balachaturbhadrika Churna (Classical Four-Herb Pediatric Formula)
remedy_text: Composed of equal parts of Musta (Cyperus rotundus), Pippali (Piper longum), Ativisha (Aconitum heterophyllum — non-toxic sweet/bitter tuber), and Karkatashringi (Pistacia integerrima). Give 250-500 mg mixed with honey (for children >1 year) or mother's milk/warm water twice or thrice daily.
ayurvedic_note: In Ashtanga Sangraha (Sutrasthana Ch. 13 Agryasangraha, p. 98: 'Ativisha sangrahaniyapachaniyasarvadoshaharanam' & Uttarasthana Ch. 2 Balamaya Pratishedha, p. 506) and Chakradatta (Balarogachikitsa), Ativisha and Balachaturbhadrika are the safest, most effective classical pediatric remedies for teething diarrhea, fever, cough, and vomiting.
